Audits · France

RGAA audit

Assess and demonstrate the compliance of your online services.

Our consultants assess your websites, intranets and online services against the RGAA, the French accessibility framework. You get a precise picture of your compliance, a prioritised action plan and the accessibility statement required by law.

Request a quoteIn detail

At a glance

Standard
RGAA, 106 criteria
For
Public bodies and companies subject to French law
Deliverables
Report, audit grid, action plan, statement
Average timeframe
3 weeks

Who is affected?

Public bodies

Central government, local authorities, public institutions and bodies entrusted with a public service mission.

Large companies

Companies with a turnover in France above 250 million euros.

Organisations covered by the EAA

E-commerce, banking, transport, electronic communications: new obligations since 28 June 2025.

What the audit includes

  1. 01Representative sampleSelection of pages and journeys that faithfully reflect your service.
  2. 02Assessment of 106 criteriaManual check of every criterion and its tests, page by page.
  3. 03Assistive technologiesChecks with screen readers, keyboard navigation and magnification.
  4. 04Report and audit gridCompliance rate, details of each failure and recommended fixes.
  5. 05Prioritised action planFixes ranked by user impact and effort.
  6. 06Accessibility statementDrafted according to the official template, ready to publish.

Frequently asked questions

How long does an RGAA audit take?

It depends on the size of the sample and the complexity of your journeys. We specify it in our proposal after a scoping call.

What is the difference between RGAA and WCAG?

RGAA is the French method for checking accessibility. It turns WCAG requirements into precise criteria and tests that an auditor can apply.

Is an audit enough to make a website compliant?

No. The audit establishes the compliance status and the action plan. Compliance comes from the fixes, which we can carry out or support, followed by a re-audit.

Must the accessibility statement be updated?

Yes. It must reflect the actual state of the service: after every major change and after every new audit.
